rationale: The claim line's billed procedure must be checked against current clinical criteria to determine medical necessity before it can be approved, denied, or escalated. This is a declared FK in procedure_catalog.csv, so retrieval is a direct lookup rather than a rule.

structured_signal_example: procedure_code = 99214 (Office Visit, Established Patient) -> coverage_policy_id = HLT-PROC-005
rationale: Some procedures route to the Medical Necessity Review Procedure rather than the Clinical Criteria document, depending on procedure_category. This shows the same FK field resolving to different document types based on the procedure being billed.

The plan booklet defines what is covered and at what member cost-share (copay/coinsurance/deductible). There is no FK for this in insurance_plans.csv, so the system must match plan_type and coverage_region to the correct benefits document rather than dereferencing a key.

structured_signal_example: plan_type = Silver HMO, coverage_region includes CA, service_start_date in 2024
rationale: HLT-POL-002 is marked authority_status = Superseded. A claim with a 2024 date of service must retrieve THIS version, not the current Gold PPO booklet, to be evaluated under the coverage terms that were actually in effect. Demonstrates that retrieval must be time-aware, not just attribute-aware.

State-mandated benefits can supplement or override the base national plan document. A claim for a CA member must additionally retrieve this addendum so a state requirement is not silently missed in favor of only the national policy.

structured_signal_example: procedure requires prior auth -> should route to HLT-PROD-01
rationale: Conceptually this linkage should exist (prior-auth status on a claim should route to the requirements matrix), but HLT-PROD-01 has authority_status = Draft.
